text:
Tess Nguyen: dropped a new microflow for Pool Affinity + Surge Cap UX. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/newflow/pool-affinity-surge. Pitch: show which GPU pool is "affinitized" to the route, surface a small 'surge cap' control (max short-term burst tokens) and surface instant p95 & cost delta inline. Keep the compact row readable on narrow dashboards. Elliot Park: Love the affordance that shows both pools when hybrid (Pinned: pool-a · Elastic: pool-b). One ask: make it obvious which pool the burst will come from. Maybe a small arrow icon from the burst badge pointing to the pool chip. Sam Ortiz: Copy thoughts: rename "Surge cap" to "Burst cap (short-term)" for clarity. Tooltip: "Burst cap controls how much spare capacity we can borrow for short bursts; higher caps may increase cost." Short tooltip for mobile: "Burst cap: controls short bursts; may affect pricing." Priya Sharma: Accessibility: the pool-affinity cluster should be a single compound control with `role=group` and `aria-label` like `Pool affinity: pinned pool-A, elastic pool-B (burst enabled)`. Don't rely on color; include icons and offscreen labels. Devon Hall: Interaction note: adding a numeric surge cap slider + stepper combo. When users change cap, run a quick estimate and show `Est. p95: 340ms · Cost: +9%` in a transient chip. For keyboard users, that same text should be pushed into an `aria-live="polite"` region. Debounce updates to 275ms. a11y-bot: Tip: use `aria-valuetext` on the burst cap thumb like `Burst cap 50% — estimated p95 340ms, cost +9%` so screen readers get context while scrubbing. Also ensure the transient chip is focusable if users open it intentionally. Tess Nguyen: edge-case: if the pinned pool is GPU-constrained (no spare), the burst cap should be disabled and show `Burst unavailable · pinned pool has no spare GPUs` with a lock icon and `aria-disabled` true. Also add a quick action `Switch to elastic` that opens the pool picker. Elliot Park: UX microcopy for disabled state: prefer "Burst unavailable on pinned pool" over "Burst disabled". Add an inline CTA link `Switch to elastic` which opens the pool selector modal. Make sure the CTA is keyboard accessible and has clear focus styles. Sam Ortiz: Visual: add a subtle safety band on the SLO slider to indicate guardrail-safe range. If a user drags outside it, show a persistent inline banner: "Guardrail alert — this SLO may push P95 above target" with actions `Auto-suggest` and `Force apply` (force apply shows consequences). Banner should persist until addressed. Priya Sharma: Keyboard flow proposal: collapsed row -> pool-affinity group -> burst cap slider -> burst cap info button -> SLO slider -> guardrail banner (if present). Info panels must be closable with Escape and focus must return to the last interactive element. Devon Hall: Implementation: recommend the surge cap slider use our existing range component but with `aria-describedby` pointing to offscreen summary. Example offscreen snippet in mock: `
Pool affinity: pinned pool-a; elastic pool-b. Burst cap 50%. Safe SLO range 200ms-500ms.
` a11y-bot: Also: ensure live region updates are debounced and suppressed when a modal is open to avoid AT flooding. Use `aria-hidden=true` on decorative icons and provide text equivalents for all icons. Tess Nguyen: question for PM/design: do we show cost estimates as percent or dollar? I prefer percent for quick scannability; dollar when you expand details. Elliot Park: Percent first, dollars in expanded panel. Add a small chevron next to the chip to reveal a micro-panel: breakdown by token type (prompt vs completion) and estimate window used for calc. Sam Ortiz: One more copy nit: for the pool picker modal header use `Select burst-capable pool` instead of `Choose pool` to communicate intent. Also show badges for pool attributes: `pinned`, `elastic`, `estimated spare GPUs`. Priya Sharma: Testing notes: run keyboard + NVDA + VoiceOver pass on the compound pool-affinity control, test with large text and 200% zoom, and verify focus order remains consistent when rows are dynamically injected (e.g., when pool list updates). Devon Hall: I'll prototype the burst-cap slider with aria attributes and the transient chip behavior. Will include focusable micro-panel and the offscreen summary. Tess Nguyen: Next steps: I'll update the figma to add the pool arrow, disabled state, and the percent-first estimate chip. Tagging @Priya for a11y sign-off and @Sam for copy review. ETA: tomorrow midday. :sparkles:
